I am a 60-year-old farmer with no schooling, but I have been working this land since I was a boy. My family has about 8 mu of good flat land in Quzhou, and I do not try fancy things — I plant what I know, what the grain station buys, and what feeds my household.

The winter wheat went into the ground last October, the way it always does. I used the rotary tiller before sowing and put down compound fertilizer as the base. I plant an improved wheat variety — maybe Shimai or Jimai — because the old black wheat does not yield enough anymore, and the seed from the co-op is not expensive. Now it is spring, and the wheat is green. I will topdress with urea at jointing, irrigate three or four times total (overwintering water was already done, now jointing water, then heading and grain-filling water), and spray for insects and fungus maybe three or four times. If the weather cooperates, I should get around 1000 jin per mu.

After we harvest the wheat in early June, there is no time to waste. I will plant summer maize right away, probably without tilling — just direct seeding into the wheat stubble. Everyone here uses hybrid seed now, one small bag per mu. It grows fast. I will put down compound fertilizer at sowing and maybe side-dress urea later when the rain comes. Two irrigations are usually enough if the summer rain is normal, and I will spray for weeds and corn borers two or three times. I expect about 1100 jin per mu from the maize.

I do not grow cotton or vegetables — they need too much labor and the market price jumps around. Wheat and maize are safe. The state buys them, and I understand them.
